messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated p95 latency observed for /v1/generate (hosted). Auto-pager triggered. Secondary channels: #eng-sre, #product, #support

alice: oncall here, looking. saw spike at ~15:04 UTC, p50 ~120ms -> p95 ~2.1s. :eyes:

ben: looking at dashboards now — sudden bifurcation around 15:03 UTC across multiple regions, but concentrated in eu-west-1.

carla: customer impact: several low-volume customers reported timeouts; support ticket 3891 and 3892 linked. embedding endpoints unaffected so far.

alice: immediate mitigation: routing policy to shift new requests away from eu-west-1 to us-west-2 for 10m. Applying now (canary 10%).

devops-bot: route-change: apply-balance eu-west-1 -> us-west-2 (canary=10%) — succeeded in 6s.

oncall-sre: can you attach a condensed timeline and top logs? I have kernel/cgroups suspicion from recent node bootstrap.

ben: grabbing traces — p95 traces show long scheduling gaps and stalls at token decode stage. sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d. span breakdown:
```
- span: token-gen (mean 40ms)
- span: scheduler-wait (p95 1.7s)
- span: nvdecode 20-30ms
```

carla: I pulled host-level perf counters for affected hosts (euw-rtg-*) — notable jump in page faults and context-switches around spike. snippet: 
```
node=euw-rtg-12
timestamp=2026-02-11T15:03:07Z
page_faults: 1245 -> 9870
context_switches/s: 320 -> 2200
runqueue_len: 24
```

alice: that matches kernel-level regressions we've seen when a kernel patch changed scheduler wake heuristics. Any recent infra deploys?

devops-bot: infra-deploy: kernel-upgrade batch-eu-2026-02-11 completed 14:58 UTC (versions: 5.19.18 -> 6.1.4-rt). A subset of eu nodes were on new kernel.

ben: correlation looks strong: nodes that received kernel 6.1.4-rt show the tail in traces and high runqueue_len. non-upgraded nodes are fine.

carla: reproducing locally with kernel-6.1.4-rt in a staging image reproduced increased preempt/resched latency under our workload. sending repro artifact to #eng-runtime.

alice: mitigation step 2: roll back kernel on a small pool and verify. Initiating targeted rollback for eu-rtg-10..14. ETA ~8m.

devops-bot: rollback-job: eu-rtg-10..14 queued, rolling in parallel (max-parallel=2).

oncall-sre: in parallel, turning on temporary prefix caching to reduce decode work for hot prompts — config change pushed to hosted runtime.

ben: logs show p95 dropping back on rolled-back hosts after ~90s post-reboot. dashboard udpate: eu-rtg-12 p95 from 2.1s -> 210ms.

carla: good — customer tickets updated, support notified. Notifying top-10 customers impacted.

ops-lead: capturing timeline:
- 14:58 UTC kernel-upgrade batch started (eu subset)
- 15:03 UTC p95 spike begins
- 15:04 UTC pager -> oncall ack
- 15:06 UTC routing canary applied (10% to us-west-2)
- 15:08 UTC trace+perf pulled, kernel correlation suspected
- 15:12 UTC targeted kernel rollback initiated
- 15:14 UTC prefix cache enabled as mitigation
- 15:17 UTC p95 dropping on rolled-back hosts

alice: next steps for in-incident RCA: collect full trace bundles (trace-0a1b2c3d and related), kernel config diff, boot logs, perf counters and runqueue profiles. Ben please assemble and post S3 bundle.

ben: uploading bundle to https://logs.redwood.ai/bundles/incident-3176543210.tar.gz (contains traces, perf, dmesg, sysctl, kernel package list). ETA 2m.

carla: adding hypothesis notes in-thread: H1: kernel 6.1.4-rt changed scheduler wake heuristics causing higher scheduler-wait under high vCPU contention -> p95 spikes. H2: memory compaction path regressions increasing page faults (less likely given embeddings unaffected). H3: unrelated workload spike — less likely (no traffic surge in metrics).

alice: assign owners: H1 -> @ben (kernel perf), H2 -> @carla (mem/proc), traces -> @alice (end-to-end). We'll add more if found.

devops-bot: bundle upload complete: https://logs.redwood.ai/bundles/incident-3176543210.tar.gz (size 45MB).

oncall-sre: sharing minimal repro command for runtime team: 
```
# reproduce scheduling tail under load
stress-ng --cpu 8 --context 200 --timeout 30s &
python load_token_decoder.py --model llama-mini --qps 50 --seq 1024
```

carla: noted. I can reproduce on local VM with kernel-6.1.4-rt and the above load. will capture perf script and flamegraph.

alice: mitigation complete: canary routing kept for 15m, then normal routing resumed once autoscaling absorbed load. All rolled-back hosts show stable latencies.

ops-lead: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~6 customers experienced degraded p95 (2-3x), 2 transient timeouts, no data loss. Support tickets: 3891,3892. Credits TBD.

ben: final in-thread note: preserved trace spans and perf counters in bundle; kernel change confirmed as strongest signal. Moving to RCA doc — I'll start a dedicated doc and link here.

alice: handing off to next oncall (carla) for overnight RCA follow-up. Carla — please publish initial RCA draft by EOD and include remediation plan (block kernel rollout, add canary check, improved perf gating).

carla: ack. will publish draft and assign follow-ups. tagging @ops-lead for timeline. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated, monitoring. Postmortem channel: #postmortems.
